items.label: Voice-Matched Outreach
items.title: Cold outreach and follow-ups, drafted in your own voice -
items.title_emphasis: I use it to book these calls.
items.description: Same style-learning engine as the content pipeline's voice engine, just pointed at outreach instead of posts. It drafts the first-touch emails and the follow-ups, and they actually sound like you wrote them, not some copy-paste template. Built it for a client first. Now it runs my own pipeline's prospecting, this site included.

items.label: Content Pipeline
items.title: Cut a 6-hour weekly content task to
items.description: One event kicks off the whole chain. Update emails and feedback requests go straight out, and the system drafts the LinkedIn, WhatsApp and Facebook posts itself, in that person's own voice, learned from a sample of what they've actually written before. Not a template. A stats page tracks how it's actually landing. The only thing a human still does is hit approve.

items.label: Tender
items.title: Reads a whole tender pack and tells you
items.description: Tender packs are huge. Dozens of documents, and someone has to read every page before they even know if it's worth bidding. So I built something that reads the lot: PDFs, Word files, spreadsheets, even scans. It pulls out the deadline, what you have to send back, the requirements and the contract risks, then checks them against your company and gives you a go or no-go. The bit I care about most is that every answer comes with the page and the exact quote it came from, and the value is re-read from that quote, not taken on the AI's word. If it can't find something, it says so. It doesn't guess. I tested it on real council tenders against a demo contractor, and it caught £2m of insurance cover against £5m required and flagged it as a hard stop, before anyone wasted a week on the bid. This is stage one. Next up is the bid writer, which checks every claim in the answer against the company's own records.
flow: Every answer quoted to its page
